causes.label: demand
causes.quote: On the day, the temperature in Adelaide reached a maximum of 38.1 °C. This drove high demand in South Australia, reaching a maximum for the day of 2980 MW at 4.30 pm. Conditions at the time saw demand up to 84 MW greater than forecast four hours ahead and around 260 MW greater than forecast 12 hours ahead.

causes.label: demand
causes.quote: The maximum temperature in Melbourne exceeded 35 °C, driving a maximum demand for the day of 9506 MW at 4 pm. Conditions at the time saw demand around 450 MW greater than forecast four hours ahead and around 730 MW greater than forecast 12 hours ahead.

causes.label: scheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: AGL's Torrens Island Power Station (TIPS) units A1, A3 and B2 were not in service for all three days, but were available with 24 hours notice.

causes.label: scheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: There were reductions in available capacity of 510 MW as a result of technical issues on 8 February.

causes.label: unscheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: At around 10.50 am, AETV Power's Bairnsdale unit two tripped (from 44 MW). The reason provided was '1045 P unit OOS et 7 hrs - SL'. The unit was out of service from 10 am and returned to service from 5.30 pm the same day.

causes.label: unscheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: Ecogen Energy reduced the available capacity at Newport power station, Jeeralang Units A and B by a total of 583 MW. These reductions were effective for varying periods, with some effective from 1.30 pm, lasting until 4 pm. The most significant reduction was for the entire 510 MW at Newport power station, with 200 MW of this capacity priced below $25/MWh.

causes.label: network_outage
causes.quote: At around 4.30 pm, following the reclassification of transmission lines in Victoria, which forced flows out of South Australia, reserves fell below the size of the largest unit and a Lack of Reserve Level 2 condition (LOR2) was declared in South Australia.

causes.label: rebids
causes.quote: There was no significant rebidding in South Australia on 8 February.

causes.label: rebids
causes.quote: At 2.56 pm, Snowy Hydro rebid Murray Power Station's ramp down rate from 200MW/min down to the minimum allowable level of 3MW/min. The reason given was '14:32:A being constrained off at Murray in 5mpd 15:00@14:30'.

causes.label: ramp_rates
causes.quote: At 2.56 pm, Snowy Hydro rebid Murray Power Station's ramp down rate from 200MW/min down to the minimum allowable level of 3MW/min. The reason given was '14:32:A being constrained off at Murray in 5mpd 15:00@14:30'.

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: Twelve hours prior to the high prices, import limits into South Australia across the Heywood interconnector were forecast at a minimum of 350 MW. This was revised up to around 450 MW 4 hours prior to dispatch. However, during the time of high prices, actual imports into South Australia were between 300 MW and 350 MW.

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: Twelve hours prior to the high prices the import limit into South Australia across the Murraylink interconnector was forecast to be 150 MW. This was revised down to around 80 MW 4 hours prior to dispatch. The actual import capability into South Australia during this time was limited to below 50 MW due to the system normal constraint V>>V_NIL_1B.

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: The import limit into Victoria across the NSW-Vic interconnector was forecast to be between 440 MW and 540 MW for the afternoon. However, the V>>V_NIL_1B constraint limited actual imports into Victoria to around 200 MW.

constraints_named.quote: The actual import capability into South Australia during this time was limited to below 50 MW due to the system normal constraint V>>V_NIL_1B.
At this time, the system normal constraint, V>>V_NIL_1B, which limits generation from the Murray Power station, was binding.

causes.quote: On Tuesday 9 February, high temperatures continued in Adelaide, reaching a maximum of 39°C.

causes.label: demand
causes.quote: The temperature in Melbourne reached a maximum for the day of 32.1 °C. Conditions at the time saw demand up to 200 MW greater that forecast four hours ahead and 270 MW greater than forecast 12 hours ahead.

causes.label: scheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: AGL's Torrens Island Power Station (TIPS) units A1, A3 and B2 were not in service for all three days, but were available with 24 hours notice.

causes.label: scheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: On 9 and 10 February, 200 MW of lower cost Victorian generation was unavailable as a result of technical issues.

causes.label: unscheduled_plant_outage
causes.quote: Over several rebids International Power reduced the available capacity of Hazelwood Power Station unit 4 by up to 215 MW. These rebids were first effective from 9.45 am. The reasons given were '0937F boiler leak', '1150P Boiler leak', '1229P Boiler leak', '1245P Boiler leak', '1319P Boiler Leak', '1343P unit outage - tube leak'.

causes.label: network_outage
causes.quote: This constraint was invoked at 4.10 pm in response to the reclassification of a non-credible contingency event on the Dederang to Glenrowan lines as a result of lightning in the vicinity.

causes.label: rebids
causes.quote: In South Australia, over several rebids first effective from 1.15 pm, AGL rebid up to 80 MW at Torrens Island from prices below $35/MWh to the price cap. The reason given was '12:31A chg in AEMO forecasts :: SA decr price $3K+'.

causes.label: rebids
causes.quote: Further rebids (shifting capacity into higher price bands and reducing low-priced available capacity) combined with lower than forecast imports saw increases in the actual spot prices compared to forecast.

causes.label: ramp_rates
causes.quote: At 2.16 pm, effective from 2.25 pm, Snowy Hydro rebid Murray Power Station's ramp down rate from 200MW/min down to the minimum allowable level of 3MW/min. The reason given was '14:16:A being constrained off at Murray'.

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: Twelve hours prior to dispatch the import limit into South Australia across the Heywood interconnector was forecast to be between 350 MW and 380 MW. This was revised to 425 MW four hours prior to dispatch. Actual imports were limited to under 350 MW during the period of high prices, with the import limit falling to approximately 180 MW at 4.30 pm.

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: Twelve hours prior to dispatch, the import limit across Murraylink into South Australia was forecast to be between 50 MW and 150 MW during the period of high prices. Four hours prior to dispatch this was forecast to be around 150 MW. However, actual import capability into South Australia between 1.30 pm and 4 pm was between 40 MW and 62 MW.

causes.label: interconnector_limit
causes.quote: From 2.10 pm until 3.30 pm, a system normal constraint restricted flows into Victoria from New South Wales across the Vic-NSW interconnector.

causes.label: constraint_violation
causes.quote: The constraint V>>SML_DDGN violated at 4.15 pm, and continued to bind through the remainder of the high-priced period.

constraints_named.quote: The system normal constraint, V^^S_NIL_NPS_SE_OFF (which limits flows on the Heywood interconnector to prevent its overload should there be a loss of one unit at Northern Power Station) was binding for most of the period.
The constraint V>>SML_DDGN violated at 4.15 pm, and continued to bind through the remainder of the high-priced period.
At this time, the system normal constraint, V>>V_NIL_1B was binding.

In addition, a quick (CA or Contingency Analysis) constraint was invoked from 3.30 pm to 7.40 pm placed further restrictions on imports into Victoria across the Murraylink and Vic-NSW interconnectors.
From 4.50 pm, the constraint set #VIC1-NSW1_E was invoked to minimise the negative settlement residues that had begun to accrue.
